memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "With each of the thirteen bulls offer a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil; with each of the two rams, two-tenths; and with each of the fourteen lambs, one-tenth. Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering." - Num 29:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The offerings for the first day of Tabernacles were lavish: thirteen bulls, two rams, fourteen lambs, each accompanied by grain and drink offerings, and a sin offering as well. This was worship on a grand and generous scale. The joy of the festival was expressed in abundant giving to God. Nothing was held back.

There is a lesson in this generosity. When our hearts are full of gratitude for what God has done, our worship becomes generous rather than stingy. The reconciled and rejoicing people of Israel poured out their offerings freely. Grateful worship does not calculate the minimum required; it gives abundantly out of love.

We recall that these particular sacrifices belonged to the old covenant and are fulfilled in Christ. We do not bring bulls and lambs. But the principle of wholehearted, generous devotion endures. God is worthy of our fullest worship, not a grudging or minimal offering of ourselves.

And even here, on the most joyful of feasts, the sin offering remained. Joy and the acknowledgment of our need for grace always go together. In Christ, whose sacrifice makes both our atonement and our joy possible, we are freed to worship generously and gladly (2 Cor 9:15). Let gratitude for His indescribable gift make your devotion abundant and your heart wholehearted.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your worship generous and wholehearted, or grudging and minimal?
2. How does gratitude shape the way you give yourself to God?
3. What does it mean that even in joy we depend on God's grace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let my gratitude make my worship generous and my heart wholehearted. Thank You for Your indescribable gift in Christ, which frees me to give myself to You gladly and fully. Amen.
